#562 is fixed and pushed, and its CI is running now; I'll report the result. Locally ty, ruff and all 1016 unit tests pass.

**What I changed on the branch:**
1. **Merged main**, which now includes #548. The only conflict was the API client pin, identical on both sides (dev122) and differing only in its spelling. `uv.lock` now matches main. This merge removed #562's five typecheck errors from the client upgrade.
2. **`external_tool_coordinate_system` is optional** in `forward_kinematics()` (default `None`, meaning no external tool). The docstring now describes the parameter. This fixes the two remaining typecheck errors in the Rerun bridge. It also keeps the public method backwards compatible: existing SDK code calling it with only joints and TCP keeps working.
3. **Three things only showed up once ty passed.** Before, CI stopped at the typecheck, so the unit tests never ran:
   - the private `_resolve_set_outputs()` had the same parameter without a default, which broke four path-trigger tests from main. It now defaults to `None` too.
   - one test expected the old `forward_kinematics` call without the new argument. I updated the expectation, because forwarding the coordinate system (here `None`) is intended.
   - an existing test now also checks that `forward_kinematics` without the argument sends no external tool.

**Live:** the 12 integration tests that use forward kinematics (collision checks, collision-free planning, trajectory cursor) pass on 172.31.10.98.

#562 is a colleague's PR. I merged main in rather than rebasing, so their history stays intact, and added my fix as a separate commit.

content.text:
No, #562 has no breaking changes for normal SDK use. Code that only calls the SDK keeps working unchanged. There's one edge case for custom robot classes and one minor behaviour difference.

**Why calls stay compatible:** every public method that got the new `external_tool_coordinate_system` parameter has it last, with the default `None` (no external tool). In `execute()` and `plan_and_execute()` it's keyword-only (after `*`). Existing calls, including positional ones, mean exactly the same as before. That covers:
- `MotionGroup` / `AbstractRobot`: `plan`, `execute`, `plan_and_execute`, `forward_kinematics`, `get_setup`;
- `MultiMotionGroup`: `plan`, `execute`, `attach`, `plan_and_execute` (one mapping per group);
- `motion_group_setup_from_motion_group_description()`.

`forward_kinematics()` was breaking before my fix today: the new parameter was required, so every existing call raised a `TypeError`. With the default `= None` that's resolved.

**Edge case: your own subclasses of `AbstractRobot`.** `AbstractRobot.plan()` and `.execute()` now always pass `external_tool_coordinate_system=...` on to `_plan()` and `_execute()`. A custom subclass that implements those two without the parameter would get a `TypeError`. In the SDK itself, both subclasses (`MotionGroup`, `SimulatedRobot`) are updated. `AbstractRobot` isn't exported from `nova` or `nova.cell`, only importable from `nova.cell.robot_cell`, so this most likely affects nobody. A release note line would be enough.

**Minor behaviour difference:** if you pass `plan()` your own `motion_group_setup` without a payload override, the SDK now always plans with a copy of it; before, it used your object directly. Your object isn't modified in either case. That only matters if code compares setup objects by identity.

**Not part of #562 any more:** the client upgrade to 26.9 and its consequence (datasets need NOVA 26.9 or newer) came to main with #548. After merging main, #562 has the same client version as main.

The 20 deleted lines in `pyproject.toml` are only blank lines.

#562's integration run is red again, but not because of #562: the same error now also appears on main.

**What fails:** typecheck, lint and unit tests pass (23 checks). In the integration suite it's the cancellation tests again. When the robot drives back home after a cancelled execution, the SDK receives a "paused by user at location 0.0" frame and aborts. The following tests then fail in setup, because the robot isn't at its start position. The third attempt ran out of the 45-minute time limit again.

**Why it's not #562:** the same error appears four times in today's release-please run on **main**, which failed. That run contains #548 but not #562. Since #548, main's integration suite is therefore unreliable too.

**What I know so far:**

| Runs | Client | With this error |
|---|---|---|
| #572, #552, #569 (2026-11-24) | 26.7.0 | 0 of 3 |
| #548 ×3, #562, main (2026-11-25) | 26.9.0.dev122 | 3 of 5 |

- Other possible causes are the CI server (today 26.8.1; yesterday's logs don't show the version, so it may have been updated) or plain timing.
- I can't reproduce it locally: 172.31.10.98 runs 26.9, and the error relates to 26.8 behaviour.

**What I'd suggest:**
1. **For #562:** another rerun will very likely pass, as it did on #548. #562 itself is clean.
2. **Separately, since main is affected:** investigate the cause. The SDK logs each execution frame at debug level, so the frame trace from a failing CI run shows exactly which frames arrive at the move home and why the filter doesn't drop them. If the CI log doesn't contain the debug output, I'd enable it for these tests.

I can't reproduce right now: 172.31.10.98 isn't reachable from here. ping times out, HTTP doesn't answer, and Python reports "Host is down". Yesterday it worked, so the instance is probably off, or the VPN connection is down. All eight loop runs failed only because of that, not because of the flake.

**What I've found so far:**
- **CI logs:** they contain no frame trace, only state transitions and deprecation warnings. So the cause can't be read directly from them.
- **The code:** while `armed` (new trajectory initialized, start not yet taken up), a "paused by user" frame **without** standstill sets `_moved = True` (`trajectory_state_machine.py`, `_handle_armed`). The next "paused by user" frame **with** standstill then counts as a completed user pause. In a one-shot execution that ends in exactly our error: "paused by user at location 0.0".
- **The tests:** they wait about 3 seconds after the cancellation and check that the robot isn't moving, so it isn't still braking. A single flickering standstill flag while the robot waits for the start is enough, though.

content.text:
Option 2 would be a small part of the lab work: one rule from `57ac81c7`, without the rest of the "robust standstill" package. Looking at the lab code also showed that my proposal was imprecise on one point.

**What option 2 takes from the lab (identical):**
- While waiting for the start (`armed`), a "paused by user" frame without standstill no longer sets `_moved`. In the lab, that branch only keeps waiting.
- `_moved` is set only by commanded progress (`_track_commanded_progress`). The controller only advances the location once it actually executes the start, so this is a command, not a measurement, and the standstill flag can't cause a false alarm.

**Where I need to correct my proposal:** I wrote "location > 0". The lab does it better: it notes the location of the first frame after the start as an anchor (`_start_anchor`), and only a change from that anchor counts as progress. This also works when the start doesn't begin at 0, e.g. resuming from a pause at 0.4. With "location > 0", a resume from the middle would count as "moved" right away, which is the same mistake again. A frame of another trajectory resets the anchor. Option 2 would adopt the lab's anchor logic as is.

**What option 2 leaves out from the lab** (about 1,400 lines in `movement_controller/`):

| Lab work | What it does | In option 2? |
|---|---|---|
| `StandstillEstimator` (`standstill.py`, 257 lines) | debounces the standstill flag with vote counts, commanded progress and measured joint movement; per-unit thresholds (rad vs. mm for linear axes) | no |
| Debounced standstill in all states | also when ending and pausing, not only before the start | no |
| `pending` state | "operation queued, start not yet sent" as its own state | no |
| Non-strict mode | follows contradicting frames with a warning instead of failing | no |
| Supervision of ignored resumes | reports a resume after which the controller only shows the old IO pause | no (belongs with pause-on-IO) |

**What that means:** option 2 fixes exactly the path behind the CI flake: a "paused by user" at the start position before the robot moved. It doesn't cover a flickering standstill flag in other states, e.g. ending a trajectory while the robot is still settling. The lab handles that with the debouncing. Those cases didn't show up in CI; they were measured on the real cell with a linear axis.

Option 2 is therefore a strict subset of PR 5. When PR 5 comes to main later, it replaces those lines with the same logic, so the two don't conflict.

My recommendation stays option 2 now, to get main's CI stable quickly, with the anchor logic taken verbatim from the lab. PR 5 then brings the debouncing. Shall I build it like that?

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _make_motion_group_state(
    standstill: bool, execute: api.models.Execute | None = None
) -> api.models.MotionGroupState:
    """Create a MotionGroupState with the given standstill and execute fields."""
    return api.models.MotionGroupState(
        timestamp=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
        sequence_number=1,
        description_revision=0,
        motion_group="mg-0",
        controller="ctrl-0",
        joint_position=[0.0] * 6,
        joint_limit_reached=api.models.MotionGroupStateJointLimitReached(limit_reached=[False] * 6),
        standstill=standstill,
        execute=execute,
    )
def _make_execute(
    trajectory_state: (
        api.models.TrajectoryRunning
        | api.models.TrajectoryEnded
        | api.models.TrajectoryPausedByUser
        | api.models.TrajectoryPausedOnIO
        | api.models.TrajectoryWaitForIO
    ),
    location: float = 1.0,
) -> api.models.Execute:
    """Create an Execute with TrajectoryDetails."""
    return api.models.Execute(
        joint_position=[0.0] * 6,
        details=api.models.TrajectoryDetails(
            trajectory="traj-123", location=location, state=trajectory_state
        ),
    )
def _running(location: float = 1.0, *, standstill: bool = False) -> api.models.MotionGroupState:
    return _make_motion_group_state(
        standstill, _make_execute(api.models.TrajectoryRunning(time_to_end=1000), location)
    )
def _ended(location: float = 2.0, *, standstill: bool = True) -> api.models.MotionGroupState:
    return _make_motion_group_state(
        standstill, _make_execute(api.models.TrajectoryEnded(), location)
    )
def _paused_by_user(
    location: float = 1.0, *, standstill: bool = True
) -> api.models.MotionGroupState:
    return _make_motion_group_state(
        standstill, _make_execute(api.models.TrajectoryPausedByUser(), location)
    )
def _paused_on_io(location: float = 1.0, *, standstill: bool = True) -> api.models.MotionGroupState:
    return _make_motion_group_state(
        standstill, _make_execute(api.models.TrajectoryPausedOnIO(), location)
    )
def _wait_for_io(location: float = 0.0) -> api.models.MotionGroupState:
    return _make_motion_group_state(True, _make_execute(api.models.TrajectoryWaitForIO(), location))
def _bare(*, standstill: bool = True) -> api.models.MotionGroupState:
    return _make_motion_group_state(standstill)
def _armed() -> TrajectoryExecutionMachine:
    machine = TrajectoryExecutionMachine()
    machine.arm()
    assert machine.is_armed
    return machine
def _executing() -> TrajectoryExecutionMachine:
    """A machine that has seen its first RUNNING frame."""
    machine = _armed()
    machine.process_motion_state(_running(0.5))
    assert machine.is_executing
    return machine
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class TestArmed:
    """Between a start and the first motion the controller publishes the parked
    ``PAUSED_BY_USER`` at standstill (level-based, robotics/wbr!2262). That frame,
    and the re-published terminal state of a resume, must not conclude anything."""

    def test_parked_frames_keep_the_machine_armed(self):
        machine = _armed()
        for _ in range(3):
            result = machine.process_motion_state(_paused_by_user(0.0))
            assert machine.is_armed
            assert not result.state_changed
            assert result.has_execute
        assert machine.pause_reason is None

    def test_standstill_dropping_before_the_discriminator_is_motion_starting(self):
        """Measured 2026-09-16: `standstill` flips to False one control cycle
        before the execute state flips from PAUSED_BY_USER to RUNNING."""
        machine = _armed()
        machine.process_motion_state(_paused_by_user(0.0))
        machine.process_motion_state(_paused_by_user(0.0, standstill=False))
        machine.process_motion_state(_paused_by_user(0.0, standstill=False))
        assert machine.is_armed
        machine.process_motion_state(_running(0.0))
        assert machine.is_executing

    def test_parked_frame_after_the_robot_moved_is_a_real_pause(self):
        """An external pause landing inside the start lag: the robot left
        standstill and is parked again without a RUNNING frame in between."""
        machine = _armed()
        machine.process_motion_state(_paused_by_user(0.0, standstill=False))
        result = machine.process_motion_state(_paused_by_user(0.01))
        assert machine.is_paused
        assert machine.pause_reason is PauseReason.USER
        assert result.state_changed

    def test_requested_pause_concludes_on_the_parked_frame(self):
        """A pause the owner asked for before the robot moved is the same frame as
        the parked shape; request_pause() tells them apart."""
        machine = _armed()
        machine.process_motion_state(_paused_by_user(0.0))
        assert machine.is_armed
        machine.request_pause()
        machine.process_motion_state(_paused_by_user(0.0))
        assert machine.is_paused
        assert machine.pause_reason is PauseReason.USER

    def test_arming_for_a_pause_concludes_on_the_parked_frame(self):
        """The owner paused before the machine ever left rest: the arm carries the
        pause request instead of resetting it."""
        machine = TrajectoryExecutionMachine()
        machine.arm(pause_requested=True)
        machine.process_motion_state(_paused_by_user(0.0))
        assert machine.is_paused
        assert machine.pause_reason is PauseReason.USER

    def test_wait_for_io_keeps_the_machine_armed(self):
        machine = _armed()
        machine.process_motion_state(_wait_for_io())
        assert machine.is_armed
        machine.process_motion_state(_running(0.0))
        assert machine.is_executing

    def test_bare_standstill_keeps_the_machine_armed(self):
        machine = _armed()
        result = machine.process_motion_state(_bare())
        assert machine.is_armed
        assert result.skip

    def test_ended_at_standstill_completes_without_motion(self):
        """A zero-length or one-cycle trajectory may never show ¬standstill;
        END is then the only completion signal and must count."""
        machine = _armed()
        machine.process_motion_state(_ended(0.0))
        assert machine.is_ended

    def test_ended_while_moving_goes_to_ending(self):
        machine = _armed()
        machine.process_motion_state(_ended(0.5, standstill=False))
        assert machine.is_ending
        machine.process_motion_state(_bare())
        assert machine.is_ended

    def test_io_pause_before_any_motion_is_a_real_pause(self):
        """No parked look-alike exists for PAUSED_ON_IO: the controller reports it
        only after a start armed with pause_on_io, also when the condition already
        held at the start (measured)."""
        machine = _armed()
        machine.process_motion_state(_paused_by_user(0.0))
        machine.process_motion_state(_paused_on_io(0.0))
        assert machine.is_paused
        assert machine.pause_reason is PauseReason.IO
        assert machine.is_paused_on_io

    def test_io_pause_while_moving_goes_to_pausing(self):
        machine = _armed()
        machine.process_motion_state(_paused_on_io(0.1, standstill=False))
        assert machine.is_pausing
        assert machine.is_paused_on_io

    def test_arm_resets_the_pause_request_and_motion_memory(self):
        machine = _armed()
        machine.request_pause()
        machine.process_motion_state(_paused_by_user(0.0, standstill=False))
        machine.process_motion_state(_paused_by_user(0.0))
        assert machine.is_paused

        machine.arm()
        assert machine.is_armed
        assert machine.pause_reason is None
        machine.process_motion_state(_paused_by_user(0.0))
        assert machine.is_armed, "a resume must not inherit the previous pause request"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Stale terminal frames after a resume
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Summary
- While the execution machine waits for a start (`armed`), only **commanded progress** marks the robot as moved: the trajectory location leaving where the first frame after the start found it. A `PAUSED_BY_USER` frame with `standstill=False` no longer does.
- The anchor is kept per trajectory id: a resume from mid-trajectory is not progress by itself, and a stale frame of the previous trajectory re-anchors instead of counting.

## Why
Since 2026-11-25 the integration suite fails intermittently on CI (NOVA 26.8.1), on main as well as on PRs: the move home after a cancelled execution in `test_motion_group_task_cancelation.py` raises `UnexpectedTrajectoryState: trajectory was paused by user at location 0.0 during one-shot execution`, and the following tests then fail their setup because the robot is not at their start.

The path that produces this error: in `armed`, one `PAUSED_BY_USER` frame without standstill set `_moved`; the next parked frame at standstill then concluded a user pause at the start location. The standstill flag can flicker for a frame while the robot waits parked; that was measured on a real cell on 2026-09-30, and the fix there (`lab/pause-auto-resume`, robust standstill) is what this PR ports. On NOVA 26.9 the frame shape does not occur at all (0 such frames in 16 local runs of the cancellation tests), so the flake is specific to 26.8.x servers.

## Benefits
- Main's integration suite is no longer red by chance; retries no longer eat the 45-minute job budget.
- On a real cell, a flickering standstill flag can no longer abort a one-shot execution before the robot moved.
- A real pause during the start lag is still detected: it comes with commanded progress.

## How
`TrajectoryExecutionMachine._track_commanded_progress()` runs on every trajectory frame while `armed`. The first frame anchors `(trajectory, location)`; a location that differs by more than `1e-9` sets `_moved`. `_handle_armed` no longer sets `_moved` on `standstill=False`. This is a subset of the robust-standstill work (debounced standstill in all states comes with that PR).

## Test plan
- [x] New unit tests: flicker on the parked frame keeps the machine armed (the CI scenario); progress is measured from the start's location (resume from 0.4); another trajectory's frame re-anchors. The first two fail with the old rule.
- [x] Unit suite on Python 3.12: 1019 passed; ruff and ty clean.
- [x] Integration on NOVA 26.9.0-180: cancellation, trajectory cursor and pause-on-IO tests, 11 passed.
- [ ] CI integration run on NOVA 26.8.1 without the flake.
